utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. Mr. Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, and good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-83-T, the Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we have the appearances for today, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours, Counsel, and everyone in and around the courtroom. For the Prosecution, Daryl Mundis and Matthias Neuner, assisted by our case manager, Alma Imamovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Defence? Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Vasvija Vidovic and Nicholas Robson for the Defence of General Delic, assisted by Lejla Gluhic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Before we call the witness, just a few housekeeping matters to deal with. Mr. Mundis, the Chamber is aware of a motion by the Prosecution for redesignation of witnesses as 92 or -- 92 bis or ter witnesses. I'm a bit at a loss as to what the value of this motion is supposed to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Let me -- let me try to clarify. It's -- basically, as I've indicated on a number of prior occasions recently, we're reevaluating in terms of the amount of time available to us in order to expedite the proceedings. And it's -- it's the Prosecution's understanding that this Trial Chamber requires us in the event we wish to re-designate a witness from viva voce to 92 bis or 92 ter that we need to seek the Trial Chamber's leave or authorisation in order to do that. And so simply what we've done by way of this motion is at this stage simply seeking leave from the Trial Chamber to re-classify or re-designate 9 previously-listed 92 -- or previously listed viva voce witnesses as 92 bis or 92 ter. We're not at this stage seeking to admit those statements under 92 bis. We're simply asking for authorisation to re-designate them to either 92 bis or 92 ter as a means of further expediting the proceedings and allowing us to and to get the evidence before the Chamber in the time allotted to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. That much I understand, Mr. Mundis. What my problem is, is you're still going to have to file in a 92 bis or ter motion for specific witnesses to motivate -- to bring in the -- the statements. And at that stage, as you -- as you rightly say in your -- in your motion, that this is not the stage for the -- for the Defence to object. They can object at that stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: At that stage --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Depending on what is before us, we may or may not decide that this witness should not be 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, this motion seems to be saying, Tie your hands behind your back and make sure that you are going to hear this witness as a 92 bis whether or not at the time the witness does or does not qualify.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me -- let me try to briefly address that point, which I completely understand. With respect to the 92 bis witnesses, obviously we need to get the statements certified before we can file them under Rule 92 bis. And so our position was simply that before we send a Registry officer and a -- perhaps a -- a member of the trial team down on a mission to certify four statements under Rule 92 bis that, we at least have the authorisation from the Trial Chamber to re-designate those witnesses under that rule. Now, that's a separate issue as to whether the Chamber ultimately accepts those statements under 92 bis and/or requires the witness to attend for cross-examination. But it's simply a point that before I send people and spend some of the Tribunal's resources doing 92 bis statements on witnesses that I -- I don't even have authorisation or -- or listed as 92 bis witnesses. I hope that was -- that was clear. We need to get the statements certified before we file them under Rule 92 bis, and that requires a Registry legal officer and a member of my trial team traveling to wherever the witness is to certify the statement. And out of an abundance of caution, we at least wanted to have those witnesses re-designated as 92 bis or potential Rule 92 bis witnesses, just as we've listed other witnesses as 92 bis, before we send people down to certify statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Again, I hear you. My problem is still not solved. You go down and get the witness certified as a 92 bis witness. It comes here. We look at everything. At that stage when he now has to come and testify, and on what is before us, we feel 92 bis is not the way to go. The resources have been spent. I don't -- I don't think that you are absolutely correct in saying that you need authorisation to determine which one -- which witness you want to make a 92 bis. You make -- you make the decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Oh --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And having taken the decision, you say, "Here is the witness. I would like him to be 92 bis for the following reasons." We get a response, and we decide.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That's absolutely -- that's absolutely fine with the Prosecution. And that's the way that we've proceeded in a -- in a number of other cases. My -- my -- and it was perhaps then my misunderstanding, based on some discussions with the -- with the legal officer, that -- that I was required to -- that I couldn't unilaterally switch from viva voce to 92 bis without the Chamber's authorisation. Perhaps I misunderstood the legal officer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. No, that's fine. Sorry, Judge. Just a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Okay. I'm sorry. Then that settles that matter, then. We are now on the same page, on the wavelength.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes. And if I could then ask further clarification with respect to the Rule 92 ter proposed witnesses. Would -- would the same --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The same. So then we will take the view, Your Honours -- I will actually withdraw this motion, if -- if -- if the Chamber allows me to do that. But I will indicate that the nine witnesses listed, so that the Defence is on notice --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We will be seeking to make applications in the near future under 92 bis or 92 ter for -- for those witnesses that we've designated. And it would therefore be our intention with respect to the 92 ter witnesses that we will under -- we will bring them here. We will then seek to have admitted into evidence their statement or statements. And then ask the questions in order to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: -- have those admitted, perhaps discuss a few documents with the witness in line with the Chamber's decision that we received yesterday, and then make them available for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So I think everyone's now on notice that that's our intention --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: -- with respect to these nine witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If I could while I'm on my feet before the witness comes in. Yesterday we received the -- the Defence motion concerning a reduction to the court schedule to four days a week. I'm sure the Chamber is well aware of that motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution will not be responding to that motion in writing. I can -- I can indicate, if -- if the Chamber would like, the Prosecution's very brief response to that orally, if that would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sure. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: -- be of assistance. Our position, of course, is that many, if not almost all of the issues raised are issues for the Trial Chamber. Having had the opportunity to review the Defence response, our comments are limited really to two or three very brief points. First of all, the Prosecution would respectfully ask that -- that in the event we were to be sitting four days a week rather than -- than five, that that obviously has no impact on the amount of overall time available to the Prosecution. We wouldn't want a decision to reduce from five days to four days to somehow negatively impact upon the amount of time available to us. The second point, of course, is -- as the Defence motion raises, obviously in the event of -- of illness or -- or a heavy workload affecting any of the Defence teams, that obviously could have a negative impact on the overall conduct of the proceedings, in terms of unexpected delays, et cetera, and we wouldn't want to be in a situation where any ill health or medical conditions of any of the Defence teams would negatively impact upon the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And what's your position on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Our position --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You support that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Absolutely. I both personally and professionally wouldn't want to see any work schedule that would have a detrimental effect on the health of any members of the Defence team or, for that matter, the accused. But, obviously, that's an issue for the Chamber to dwell upon. And the final point, as I've indicated in a discussion with Mrs. Vidovic, which is reflected in the final paragraph of their motion, if - and I stress the word "if" - the Chamber decides to go to a four-day week schedule, we would respectfully ask that the Trial Chamber not sit on Mondays for the simple reason that if we were not to sit on Mondays, that day could be used by the Prosecution to proof witnesses. In other words, we would fly the witnesses in on Sunday, proof them on Monday for testifying on Tuesday. If the Chamber, on the other hand, were to say, let's not sit on Fridays, that's of no assistance to us because VWS will not bring the witnesses in on Thursday to testify on the following Monday. That's simply too long of a period for the witnesses to sit in the hotel. So we could take advantage of having a Monday off to proof for Tuesday, but having a Friday off does not allow us to proof witnesses on that Friday for the following Monday because VWS will not bring the witnesses in and have them sit here over the weekend. So we would simply ask that if the Chamber opts for a four-day trial week that Monday be the day that we not sit. For that simple reason; it would save some resources and it would make -- make things move a little bit more productively.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Those are all we really have to say with respect to that motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much, Mr. Mundis. I don't imagine you have any issue to raise on this matter. The motion is going to be withdrawn.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: The motion has been withdrawn, Your Honour. What I would just say is that we would encourage the Prosecution to prepare as quickly as possible, if they're going to send team members down to Bosnia, to -- to collect declarations in order to prepare a Rule 92 bis decision --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Motion. I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The -- the other thing, just to mention for the record, Mr. Mundis, in terms of the calculation of the Prosecution hours for presenting their case, they've just gone over -- just over 50 per cent. Just to make you aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm absolutely aware of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And I track that on a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're tracking that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: -- hour-by-hour basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Right. And although you've gone over 50 per cent of your hours, you have not gone over 50 per cent of your witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'm well aware of that fact as well. And I'm also very well aware of the overall percentage of the number of the exhibits that are on our exhibit list --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: -- versus the number that have been admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So I'm happy that I took a statistics course in college for that very reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, while you are on your feet - I'm still addressing you - the Chamber is aware of a motion by the Prosecution for submission of an expert report by Ms. Brkic. The Prosecution intends to call this witness on the 26th of October. The motion was filed on the 25th of September. The -- the Defence has -- is entitled to 30 days to answer. That's just a day after the 30 day. In which case, it doesn't leave the Chamber any -- an opportunity to make a decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Again, based on discussions that I've had with the Defence teams, it's clear to me their position is that they will want to cross-examine this -- this expert. And so I'm proceeding on the basis that -- that she will need to come and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand. But they have -- they have 30 days within which to give you notice that whether -- whether they object to her qualifications or what have you. And if in line with what they told us the other day they decide to sit the 30 days before they give you that response, then --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Then we'll reschedule her, obviously if that's the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Unless you can get privately an undertaking from your colleagues on the opposite side that they'll respond quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Right. I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. I think those were all the housekeeping matters that we wanted to raise. The witness may be called in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just want to take advantage of the break to remind you that I have to follow the proceedings and listen to the witness in French, and I would please ask you to therefore make a pause between the questions and the answers and generally between all the interventions. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Hasanagic. As always, I remind you that you are bound --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- to the declaration you made at the beginning of your testimony to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. Thank you very much. I hope you've had a restful night. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Hasanagic.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday we stopped at the issue of prisoners of war. I'm going to ask you several more questions about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may the witness be shown MFI 480.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see, Witness, this document and do you recall the Prosecutor showing you this report from the 328th Mountain Brigade? I would like you to take a look at it again, and do you agree that it bears the date the 13th of September, 1995? And I'm going to ask you to memorise this date. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it, but I said that I did not remember this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But I want you to remember this date.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And there is mention that this is sent to the command post of the 35th Division.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this is the command post of the 35th Division in Zavidovici? Is that so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Take a good look at this first page of this document.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree -- and I believe that the Bosnian version is seen in its entirety. Do you agree that on the first page there is no mention that this document has been sent to anybody else but to the KM of the 35th Division? I mean in terms of dispatching or receiving rubber stamp. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: There is no markings on the top of the document that this document was sent as a coded message. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You can see the figure "284" in the corner, in the Bosnian version -- oh, you don't have it. Could the page be scrolled up, please. Right. Thank you. Can you see this figure, 284?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That figure does not indicate that this document either left the command post of the 35th Division or that it was received there. It doesn't indicate that. It could be an archiving number or something like that. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And now please take a look at the last page of the document. Take a good look at it, please. Do you agree that there is only the stamp and the signature of, ostensibly, Fuad Zelkic? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can we turn it -- can we see the whole of the document. Do you agree when documents are delivered anywhere, on the bottom left corner it should state "delivered to," and then a list, "35th Division," the archive, et cetera, et cetera? Do you agree that there are such markings on documents?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. They have.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that in this case there is no mention that the document has been delivered anywhere, on the last page of this document?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree there is no such indication.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: By the same token, there is no indication that this document was ever received by the 35th Division either through an encoded message or in any other way. There is no indication of that. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In connection with this, I would like to ask you this: Please, would you agree or accept that during the Operation Farz reporting did not work well?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were disruptions because of combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that in terms of regularity of reports and their regular frequency, there was some correspondence between you and the units concerned and the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The 3rd Corps highlighted problems in terms of reporting from subordinate units, and you forwarded that report to the subordinate units. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The situation in the field was chaotic because of the presence of numerous and various units on the ground; is that so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is so when combat operations start.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me go back to the issue of the command post of Zavidovici. You said that this was your command post. The command post of Zavidovici, as early as the end of August 1995, was constantly shelled. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All officers are -- let me rephrase. All officers went out in the field together with you during the Operation Farz so that they can join in combat activities. When I say "all officers," I mean the officers of the 35th Division; meaning you and the other officers of the 35th Division left the command post to take part in combat operations during the Operation Farz out in the field. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 99 per cent did go out in the fields. There was a handful of them left back at Zavidovici to maintain communications with the command post.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me who was left behind, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mobilisation and replenishment organ was there, because we needed to replenish our units; supplies and finances personnel; and the legal officer or the lawyer was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for this explanation. Do you agree that all operatives were out or operating officers were out in the field with you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the operatives are those who receive reports from the subordinated units through the operations centre?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, during the Operation Farz, those operatives did not sit in the headquarters of the command but were out in the field. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I am going to revisit the issue of you. On the 6th of September, 1995, if you remember, you were already at the IKM Babilon of the 35th Division; am I right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 9th of September. On the 6th of September, the order for all officers to move the command post and go to the field was signed and produced.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for this explanation. So from the 9th of September, 1995, the forward command post of the 35th Division Babilon was operational. Do you agree that it was exposed to constant unrelentless shelling from the very beginning it started operating?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the forward command post is located along the main axis so that we can do as much as we can to ensure that the combat operations and missions are accomplished, and this is why it is placed there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the extent of the shelling was such that there -- it was decided for the forward command post to be relocated? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because of the shelling and because of the progress of our combat activities, I decided further and subsequent forward command posts, which will ensure that we can control combat activities in an easier and a simpler manner.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the witness see PT2564, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please take a look at this document. You agree, don't you, that this document was produced by the command of the 35th Division at the IKM Babilon on the 11th of September, 1995?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If we can scroll down the document so that the witness can see the signature. Can you confirm this is yours?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you read the sentence below the word "I order." Do you agree that this document orders that during the 12th of September, 1995, by 12.00 the IKM of the 35th Division is supposed to be set up and occupied in the area of Livade?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So on the 11th of September, 1995, you are not residing neither in the command post of Zavidovici but you are occupying the IKM of Babilon; is that so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you said yesterday that this was located on the 12th kilometre from Zavidovici; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that in such wartime conditions, this is a long distance?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, particularly because there was combat activities and this whole area was being shelled.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: A long distance from where?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From Zavidovici, Your Honours. This is what I asked the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you understand, Witness, me asking you about the long distance from Zavidovici under such wartime circumstances?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is how I understood it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, by your leave, may this document be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 501.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May the witness be shown document D427, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please take a look at this document. Do you agree that you can see your signature?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that this is a document dated the 13th of September, 1995 produced at the forward command post of Babilon at 11.30?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me remind you of the order of the 328th Brigade that we saw a couple of minutes earlier. May the Bosnian version be scrolled down, please, and turn -- and the page 2 of this document in the English version be turned. And you recall while we were discussing the MFI document -- rather, the report of the 328th Brigade, and you do agree with me that when a document is delivered, it should have the indications in the bottom left corner about the addressees and those that it was delivered to? Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is what was lacking in the document purporting to be a report of the 328th Brigade to your command. Do you agree that the indications in the bottom left corner were missing?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I'm going to revisit the contents of this document. Please focus on item 6, and it is seen on the top of the page in the English version. Witness, please take a look at item 6.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that it is clearly stated here that "The commander of the 329th Brigade should report to the IKM of the 35th Division in the Rudace area on the 14th of September, 1995 to receive his mission?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the commander of the 329th Brigade is supposed to report at the IKM and they were in the region of Rudace village.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So on the basis of this document, I infer that on the 13th of September, 1995 you were still at the IKM of the 35th Division entitled "Babilon," but on the subsequent day, on the 14th of September, 1995, you were supposed to be in the region of the area of the Rudace village, at the new forward command post.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because combat operations were nearing Blizna and this was one of the key features after Podsijelovo and Paljenik.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, after 11.30 on the 13th of September, 1995, you were in transition towards Rudace in terms of relocating your IKM.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So on the 13th of September, 1995, you certainly were not at the KM of Zavidovici.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not in Zavidovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. May this document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 502.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we put this document away and may the witness be shown document D428.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, this is a brief document. I can see you reading it. Do you agree that this document of the 35th Division dated 16th of September, 1995, as it's stated here, was produced at the forward command post of Rudace?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You saw the signature. Is it yours?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So this document is entitled "Order on relocating the IKM." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So it is evident that on this day, on the 16th of September, 1995, you issue an order from Rudace, from the forward command post of Rudace; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you again order that the forward command post be moved or relocated; is that so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We had to follow the front line combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. So, Witness, it's true, is it not, that during this period from the 11th of September to the 16th of September, when another order to relocate the IKM, that you were constantly on the move in the northerly direction and that you were not sitting somewhere waiting for a report. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was never sitting at an IKM, at one place. I was following the combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Your operatives, were they with you following the combat activities?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Part of them were at the IKM, at the forward command post, and some of them were out in the fields with the units.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you say they were at the IKM, that means that they were at one of the IKMs that we saw being mentioned in the documents.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By your leave, may this document be given an exhibit number, Your Honours, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 503.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like you to have a look at another document, as well, D429, please. Could this document please be removed so that we can have D429 displayed. Witness, could you please have a look at the date on this document. And what it says in the heading is "The command of the 35th Division." And the date is the 17th of September, 1995. And am I right if I conclude that it is only on this day that you were at the command; that before that, you were not issuing orders from the command?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't in Zavidovici at the command either. The command of the 35th Division did not write when -- or, rather, where the document was created. He did not state the location where the document was created.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I understand. In other words, even then you were not in the division -- or rather, the division command. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Please take a look -- or rather, can we scroll down the document so the witness can see the signature. Right. Your Honours, it's on page 2 of the English version. So please take a look at what we discussed a few moments ago when we were discussing MFI 480, document -- the document of the 328th Division -- Brigade. The 328th Brigade. You remember that document, don't you? Remember this document as well. So on any document you submit, it says "to" and we see who copies were sent to.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was compulsory.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could this document please be assigned an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 504.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness -- Could this document please be removed, as well, because I'd like to move on to a different topic with this witness. Could the witness now look at MFI 461, please. You do recall, Witness, that the Prosecutor showed you an order to attack from August 1995. You do remember that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Then you said that that was not an order that you had signed -- or rather, you said that it was not a final order. Remember that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like us to review this document. Could the witness please see page 3 of this document. In English, it is page 5. Page 5 in English, please. I am sorry, Your Honours. Page 4 of the Bosnian version. Page 4. Before we move on to this page, Witness, do you agree that there are some handwritten additions to this page that we are looking at now?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a working document. It's not a final document. And that is why there are things there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Could you please show page 4 of the Bosnian version and page 5 of the English version. Page 5 in English, please. Thank you very much. Witness, could you please have a look at 5.2. So under 5.0, it says: "Tasks issued to subordinate units." And then under 5.2, there is a certain text. Could you please focus on the handwritten portions of this document, please, so that the witness can see. Could it please be zoomed in a bit. Or rather, could the document be moved so that the witness can see the handwritten text in its entirety. Thank you. Now it is visible. Do you agree that here next to 5.2 it says: "Give concrete tasks for securing" -- or can you read it, Witness?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says: "Give concrete tasks for securing lines." That is why we were in charge of securing the newly established lines.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. I hope that it exists in the English translation, Your Honours. We are discussing this handwritten note. Unfortunately, this PT doesn't have it here, but I would like the witness to confirm it, because I don't see this in the English document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: There's a problem, because the English document says at 5.3: "The El Mujahedin Detachment with 600 soldiers," then it says "handwritten above." So...

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes. Your Honours, let's make this crystal clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This handwritten addition stands parallel to 5.2; is that right, Witness?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, Witness, could you please look at 5.3 a bit. And before we focus on this paragraph, Witness, please, do you agree that this handwritten note obviously indicates that work is still being done on this document, that this is not the final version?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is not the final version.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, over here it says: "5.3. The El Mujahedin Detachment." And then it says: "With 600 soldiers." And above it says: "Whose forces are these?" Is that right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So here it is also evident that the document is not clear and that it is still being worked on; right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, could you please look at paragraph 5.4. That is the next page in both versions, I believe. Witness, please look at 5.4 now. Again, there is a handwritten addition. What is added is -- it is stated: "With 300 soldiers." And then above, in hand: "Whose forces?" That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I just want to ask you something: Do you recognise the handwriting? Whose handwriting is this? Can you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recognise it, but it must be the chief of staff in terms of the corrections made before this reached me.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, can we have a look at 5.4 and 5.5. And do you agree that next to both of these paragraphs it says "no," "no"?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you that we move on to paragraph 11; that is, page 10 in the Bosnian version and 12 in the English version. Witness, please pay attention to 11.1, "Information on demonstrated and anticipated enemy activity," and then "security support," and then "information on demonstrated and anticipated enemy activity." That's it, 11.1. Could you read it to yourself, please. I just want to put one question to you in relation to that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that war -- prisoners of war or the Geneva Conventions are not mentioned in a single word here?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. So you said that this was not a final document when you were answering the Prosecutor's questions, and that's what you said today as well.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I just want to say for the transcript that as for the 65 ter list, under number PT2449 there is a version identical to this but without the handwritten notes. I want to say this for the transcript. The same version that this witness saw here. I don't want to waste any time by displaying that version as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, anyway I just want to ask you about the procedure involved concerning these orders so that it is perfectly clear to all of us here in the courtroom. So you prepare -- you prepare a document like this. It was an order to attack. And then you submit it to the 3rd Corps for their approval. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In such situations, when a higher command approves an order, then it is valid and applicable -- or rather, only the approved order is applicable and valid. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And do you agree that this has to be clearly stated on the document itself?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It has to be signed and it has to have a stamp.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Right. And it has to say "approved"; right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we remove this document now. I would like the witness to look at document D432. Could the document please be focused.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, now I'd like to ask you whether you recognise this document.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So this is a plan that the 3rd Corps approved to you for Operation Farz; right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the upper left-hand corner, it says "I approve," and then the name of the person who approves.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in the lower right-hand corner, there is your name and signature. Is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at page 2 of this document now. This page 2 roughly has the same content. On the top, there is the approval and name of the commander of the 3rd Corps. Can we just see the bottom of this page in Bosnian so that the witness can see it. Is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let us just have a look at the date. The date can still be seen up here; is that right? So this order of yours was approved on the 25th of August, 1995 at 1500 hours; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now could you briefly look at the next page of both versions, please. Could we please have this document focused so that we see the upper right-hand corner, please. What I want to ask you, Mr. Hasanagic, is the following: Do you see this stamp here?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that every page of approved orders has to be verified with a stamp?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In this case, there are several variants that are prepared beforehand and we have to know what the final version is by way of this stamp that is then affixed on each and every approved page.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. So the stamp shows that that is the final version, the valid version, the approved version; right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now I would like us to look at page 6, please, in Bosnian; page 7 in the English version, Your Honour. Could you please have a look at this part, "Tasks issued to subordinate units." And please look at paragraph 5.3, where the El Mujahedin Detachment is mentioned that we saw a few moments ago. You remember that something completely different was written here, 500 or some big figure? 500, 600? Do you agree that there is no such thing in this order?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you to look at paragraph 11, that refers to security support and self-protection. Page 11 of the Bosnian version and page 13 of the English version. Witness, please, Mr. Hasanagic, take a look and read this section where it says "Security support and self-protection." Take a look at the second, third, and fourth paragraph. Second, third, and fourth paragraph, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the fourth paragraph of this section continues on the following page in the English version, so please give us a sign when we are supposed to turn the page.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You recall that we were taking a look at the version of the order shown to you by the Prosecutor. Please, can we have the next page in the English version. So, Witness, do you agree that this part of the order contains something completely different under this heading than the previous one?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Here it is clearly stated what are the instructions as -- with regard to the reception of prisoners of war, and they are demanded to be handed over to the members of military police. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also what is demanded is that prisoners of war be treated in the spirit of the Geneva Conventions. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What is demanded is that elderly and very young prisoners of war be treated with special care; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now please take a look at the last page of the document, both versions, the Bosnian and the English. We can see your signature. Please confirm whether this signature is yours.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Hasanagic, I'd like to ask you this: This document that I showed you is a photocopy of the original document; is that so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is my order.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this document has been certified and verified and approved by the command of the 3rd Corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So the document showed by the Prosecutor under MFI 461, although bearing your signature, is not a copy of the original of the approved version of the order to conduct Operation Farz; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could, Your Honours, please this document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 505.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Madam Vidovic, while we are here, you are four minutes from making up the time that the Prosecution took.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that I need 15 minutes tops. I am very close to concluding my cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, while we are still with this document, I'm just curious to know - it may not be relevant, but I'm curious to know - on whose initiative was the reference to the Geneva Conventions included in the final Farz plan? I'm asking because you drew our attention to the fact that in the draft, there was no reference to the Geneva Conventions and no specific order to treat the prisoners of war in accordance with the Geneva Conventions, but now in the final plan such a provision has been included. Who initiated this inclusion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the working plan, there were proposals and it contains many other elements. And in the final version, the chief of staff and other people from the commander, together with the chief of security, we included all these elements here. So the -- it was our initiative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Could I be more specific and ask you if your lawyer was involved in this? Because I heard you mention that there was a lawyer attached to your Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The security organ, the lawyer, chief of staff, chief of the operative organ, and I. This is the group of officers that finalizes this document and all other major documents. There is mention of a group for document preparation, comprising the people I just listed, and they're in charge of determining the final version of all major and important documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I'd briefly like to address certain other documents shown to you by the Prosecutor, so could we see Exhibit 432 appear on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Exhibit 432?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's just that the previous document was document 432. I'm just wondering if you're not making any ...

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the Bosnian version as it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, the Prosecutor showed you this document. It seems that this goes for a document of the 35th Division's command. The date is, it seems, some day in April 1995. But what I'd like to ask you is this: Please -- Can we have the display as it is in the Bosnian version. Please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just -- I hear you saying the date is a day in April sometime in 1995. I see the English version says "August." Can we just make sure that it's April and not August.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it is very illegible on this version. I can't make out the date here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then let's not say "April."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I wanted to say: I would rather say it was 04, 1995 or the fourth month. But that's not the point of my question. Something else, as you will see for yourselves, Your Honours, is the point of my question.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you agree that you can make out the figure "42", centre top? Could you explain to the Bench what is written here?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Not an original."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So this is the document shown to you by the Prosecutor, this document that we can see before us. Doesn't this note, "not an original," indicate that this is not an original? How else would you interpret those words?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somebody wrote "not an original," but it would require further analysis for us to see what it is all about.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. When you confirmed to the Prosecutor that this was an order for a certain attack, did you perform such an analysis in the way that we applied our analytical skills on the previous document, did you analyse this document, given that it bears a notation "not an original"?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not. It was just shown to me as is. I did not have the time to perform any analysis.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. It means that can you claim that this order is an original, not having analysed it and -- since this is a photocopy, and given that it bears the notation "not an original"?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm really confused, to be frank. I can't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let's make this situation clear. Are you confused by my question or the --

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will repeat my question. Witness, please, what is stated here is "not an original." My question was: Given that you confirmed, asked by the Prosecutor, that this was your order, now I'm asking you: Are you sure that this is your order, even when it's stated here "not an original"?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it bears my signature on the last page, then this is my order, because I signed it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, please, do you agree that the signature on the previous document - that was MFI 461, shown to you by the Prosecutor - that that document bore your signature but having analysed it, you stated that this was not ordered? Can you claim that this order is yours, regardless of the fact that it bears your signature, by the same token?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You did not analyse it very carefully when shown by the Prosecutor, did you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, maybe I will have five to ten minutes after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. Then we'll take the break and come back at quarter to 11.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may we have the witness see PT21 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel repeat the number, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] PT2132. Thank you. For the record, this is a document of the command of the 3rd Corps produced at Zenica on the 2nd of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please take a look at it. First of all, do you agree that the document bears the title "Activating the El Mujahedin Detachment in the area of responsibility of the 35th Division"?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at item 2 of this order.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this would be on the following page in the English version. May we see the signature, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise this signature?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the signature of the corps commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Item 2 says: "The re-subordination is to be implemented from the 2nd of June until needed and until the present order has been changed." So do you agree that this order concerns the re-subordination of the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may we admit this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 506.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Madam -- Madam Vidovic, before we take away this document from the screen, I would like you to clarify from where the El Mujahid Detachment was re-subordinated. We understand that it -- it was now re-subordinated under the 35th Division, but where was it before? Under whose command was it before that?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, if you can answer this question. Can you answer His Honour's question? I will refresh your memory as to the follows so that we can try to answer this question. First help me. When was the 35th Division established?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 1st of March, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Do you recall that on the 31st of March, 1995 the El Mujahedin Detachment was re-subordinated to the 35th Division?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, could you explain to the Bench what happened to that detachment between the 31st of March and the 2nd of June, 1995. Where was it, who they were subordinated or re-subordinated to.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The El Mujahedin Detachment is a unit of the 3rd Corps. Their command post is in Zenica. They were part of the composition of the 3rd Corps. And by these orders, they were re-subordinated for the effectuation of concrete, specific missions. And it can be seen from this decision -- this order, rather, that the commander determined which missions they are going to accomplish in my area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Do you agree that the commander said here: "The re-subordination is to be implemented from the 2nd of June, 1995 until needed and until the present order has been changed"? So he suggests that this is to be so until the order is changed.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the right of the commander who re-subordinated a unit to take it and use it for some other purposes because that unit is part of his establishment or until the mission has been accomplished for the purpose of which that unit was re-subordinated.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, does this answer satisfy your curiosity or shall I dwell further on this issue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: It does indeed. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I just make a technical announcement. This document was just tendered as Exhibit 506. The Prosecution believe -- believes it has been tendered earlier as Exhibit 396 already. If this could please be checked maybe by the registrar. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It wasn't clear to us either. It seemed that ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah. But 396 was PT -- P02133. Now this is 2132. If we can be clear as to whether -- whether P02133 and PT2132 are the same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: There might be the possibility that this current document, which is P506 -- Exhibit 506, has a different ERN number but is indeed referring to the same document. So that -- we have two of the same documents but with different ERN numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Why -- why don't we have a look at the document 2133.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I can be of assistance. It is the same document, I see here now; however, the problem is that there are quite a few documents that the Prosecution -- well, you know, you can find one document under two or even three PT numbers. The very same document. That's what creates the confusion. Now when I look at the form of this document, it differs from the form of the other document that I showed today. However, the content is the same. Believe me, we are not in a position to follow then what it was that was admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I appreciate what you say, Madam Vidovic. At the same time, we just don't want to burden the record with a duplication of documents of -- which are saying the same thing. If the difference is only in form and not in substance, do we need to admit this document if it's already admitted?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely not, Your Honour. No. I would not have tendered it otherwise. So I withdraw my request to have this document admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. Then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: We are sure it's the same?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, both parties are assuring us that it's the same. We haven't seen 2133 yet. If -- maybe you'd like us to see 2133, we can do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we be shown 2133, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. It has the same number. And there are no additions that would make it any different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. In that -- in that event, then thank you very much for withdrawing the tendering of this 5 -- 2132. Thank you very much. Mr. Registrar, will you reserve number 506 for the next exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness just have a look at D434, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please have a look at this document. It's a very short one. Could you please have a look at the signature. Do you see it?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this document was created at the forward command post of the 3rd Corps Natron?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the 23rd of September, 1995, operative time, et cetera, and the heading says: "Withdrawal of the El Mujahedin Detachment from the structure of the 35th Division." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to draw your attention to paragraph 1. It says: "Order of the commander of the 3rd Corps on the re-subordination of the El Mujahedin Detachment to the 35th Division is hereby annulled and the El Mujahedin Detachment is placed under the direct command of the 3rd Corps command." So, please, is it correct that on the 23rd of September - that is to say, the 23rd of September - the order on the re-subordination of the El Mujahedin Detachment to the 35th Division was annulled?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what is written here.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Except for the fact that it's written here, is it something that actually did happen? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the details.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is possible?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions for this witness. And could this document please be assigned an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 506.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner, any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. I would like to deal with the request from Judge Harhoff during the cross-examination that the Prosecution addresses the July orders issued by the General Staff. And in order to do that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner, I really apologise for interrupting you, but when you speak and Mr. Mundis is busily typing on his keyboard, that really does compromise the -- the -- the quality of -- of your voice. I wonder if -- if Mr. Mundis could move over to another keyboard or -- or be less active on the -- thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. I want to talk briefly about the July orders as issued by the General Staff and as discussed by my learned colleague yesterday. If we could please, with the assistance of the usher, have Exhibit 443 as a point of departure being shown. And while this is being done, could you, Mr. Hasanagic, tell the Court briefly, which combat operation, if any, was launched in July 1995 by the 35th Division?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in July 1995 that the operation started and Krcevine, Gaj, and Malovan were the features that were to be taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. If you look here at the document. You remember having been shown that document by both parties, I believe, in the last days?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And we can see it relates to the 18th of July, 1995. And I'm interested in the first line again. We find here two orders being mentioned: An order by the General Staff - and I'm just reading out the last four digits - 1306, dating from 17th of July; and another order from the 3rd Corps command, 501 are the last three digits here, from the same day. Is it correct that during the course of the last five days you have not seen the -- the 3rd Corps order?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Therefore, I want to turn my attention to the General Staff order. 1306 were the last four digits. If we could briefly move to Exhibit 496, please, which was shown yesterday, bearing the last four digits in mind, 1306. If this is enlarged as it is done now. If you look at the last four digits of this order. Could you read them out for the record, please.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What digits? I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: 1 -- I will do it for you, 1 -- the Broj number, 1/825-1276. Can you follow me?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In the document we just saw a moment ago, were these digits mentioned or not?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes. Indeed the report we saw a moment ago refers to a different Broj number than the one order we have here in front of us; correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yeah. Nevertheless, I want to draw your attention to one aspect of number 1. If we could scroll the English version down. And we see here, if I can quote: "Immediately undertake all necessary activities to activate the whole front on the battlefield of RBiH ...." What would you understand would that mean, "to active the whole front on the battlefield"?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That we should all be active in the entire theatre of war of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and to have activities carried out within the scope of the possibilities of all the units involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I would show you a map for a second, please. With the assistance of the usher, this is map 3 from the court binder. My question to you is: Do you agree with me that the entire Bosnia-Herzegovina is being depicted here?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And the order which is currently in front of you refers to Zepa and Srebrenica, the area.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here: "In the entire theatre of war of Bosnia-Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. So where would you understand the words "entire theatre" of Bosnia-Herzegovina? What would they mean? Where should combat operations be launched, according to this map?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 1st Corps, the 5th Corps, the 7th Corps, the 3rd Corps, the 2nd Corps, the 4th Corps, down there; that is to say, in all parts of the theatre of war or front of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. If we turn now to the next exhibit. It's -- the map can please remain there. It's Exhibit 496, which was shown yesterday. Sorry, 495. My -- oh, is this 495? Hmm. Then I have only the PT number available. I apologise for this. I think I selected the wrong exhibit. The PT number is 2253 -- or the Exhibit number is 494. I apologise. 494, not 495. Yes. If you please look at the Broj number in the upper left-hand side. Do you recognise this Broj number of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And this is indeed the number to which your report issued on the 18th of July was referring to; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yeah. And if we look here at the first lines, it talks about the situation in Zepa. Could you on the map indicate where Zepa is.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that area exactly, because I was not in the area, but it's around here. [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you roughly encircle where you believe that Zepa is.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. From Srebrenica and then to the west, somewhere around here. [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you mark --

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not sure. I am simply not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you make a "1" next to the circle where you believe that Zepa is.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. And then could you tell the Chamber in which corps' AOR Zepa is lying.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was the 2nd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. So you believe Zepa is in the 2nd Corps AOR. If you look now at the order which is in front of you --

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you that I wasn't sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know what the areas of responsibility of the corps were. I cannot assert that it was the 2nd Corps. I think so, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you look at the order which is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I -- yes. Can you assert, Mr. Hasanagic, that Zepa was not in the area of responsibility of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was not in the area of responsibility of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So if you please look for a moment at the order which is in front of you. You see it is issued to the 1st, 3rd, 4th, and 7th Corps of the ABiH. Could you explain where the headquarters of these corps -- of these four corps were by indicating on the map where they are.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first one was in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you mark a "2" where you believe that Sarajevo is, for the 1st Corps.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 3rd Corps, Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you mark it with a "3".

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. 4th Corps?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 4th Corps? In Mostar. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. You marked it with a "4", yes. And the 7th Corps?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I think it was in Travnik. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. If you could mark where you believe that Travnik is with a "5".

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. So if we look at the order, especially the addressee field, we see that the order is issued to the commanders of the corps which you have indicated on the map with number 2 to 5; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am sorry, I didn't really hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you look at the order, 4 -- Exhibit 495 in front of you, you see that it is sent to the corps commands which are in the cities which you have marked with 2 to 5; correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And if you look at number 1, you see similar language to the previous order. It says: "Immediately undertake active combat operations on the entire front."

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you explain how you understand that order. Where is -- where are active combat operations ordered?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
