utterances.text: In all areas of responsibility of the units referred to here; that is to say, all units that are within these corps. They were ordered to act within the scope of their possibilities in their zones to take combat activities in order to tie up enemy forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So and then it says here, above the "order" -- above the word "order," it states: "The goal of providing that assistance would be to relieve the front around Zepa." Do you find that portion?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you explain how combat in the AORs of the 1st, 3rd, 4th, and 7th Corps relieve the front around Zepa.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite simply, all of us, as many of us as there were, were to tie up the enemy forces. The enemy did not have that many people either, but the point was to weaken their position at Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you explain again that relationship between combat in the corps' AOR, on the one hand side, and as you just stated, "weaken their position at Zepa." Whose position at Zepa would be weakened?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was referring to enemy positions, because they had to have their forces tied up with us, and then they would have less troops to send to Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So which enemy army are you referring to or enemy positions you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am referring to the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. And how would VRS forces being tied up with "us," as you just said?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A part of the forces that are moving toward Zepa and that are attacking Zepa. If we were to open even more fronts, then they would have to tie up more of their forces with us and they would have to deal with us, our forces. I am referring to the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina that was at Zepa.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's Note: We can hardly hear the witness because of the typing coming from other microphones. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So can you please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We can still hear some typing somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. So I want to move on to number 4 of the order in front of you. I think in the English it's page 2. And it says here: "Send me a report regarding this order by 20.00 hours on 18th of July, 1995, with a detailed description of activities." This order was issued on the 17th of July, as we can see, and you see the deadline. What type of deadline is given here for the completion of the task? Could you explain?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is an obligation of the corps, and I wouldn't know what those obligations were.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I understand. I'm just asking you: If the order is dating from the 17th of July and the deadline provided in number 4 is the next day at 8.00 p.m., what do you think, what type of order is this? How big or how small would you assume is the deadline or the time period provided for the implementation of this order?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I am saying I don't know. This was addressed to the corps command. What kind of reports they were supposed to submit, I really cannot answer this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me understand your question, Mr. Neuner. Are you saying the witness must tell you whether the deadline given is sufficient to accomplish the objective of the order?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes. I was trying to establish whether there is enough time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's right. That's what I'm asking. Then make sure that you -- your question is so clear to the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- that he's able to understand what you want to accomplish.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: For the purpose of launching active combat operations, which is the topic of this order, is the deadline of less than --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: For the purpose of relieving Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: -- for relieving Zepa by launching combat activities on other fronts, is the deadline of 48 hours sufficient?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Any activity is welcome to have the forces tied up.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to look with you at Exhibit 443 again, in terms of seeing whether the deadline was complied with. We see here in the second line --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. Here the Prosecutor is trying to tie up two things which have nothing in common with one another. The order dated the 18th of July being shown to the witness was sent obviously to the corps, and the other order that the Prosecutor seeks from the witness to testify whether deadlines had been honoured or not is a document produced by the 35th Division. I object to bringing those two documents in a connection where there isn't one, and this is the gist of my objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I can explain that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Please respond to that objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes. First of all, the order shown is referring to, in the first line, to the document just seen -- just shown before, 1306, the General Staff order. And we see a second document, an order for the 3rd Corps mentioned in the second line here, and we see the date of that order. And that's all I am trying to establish, the temporal relationship. We have established that the order of the General Staff, as is stated here in the first line, is from the 17th of July, and we see then the order of the 3rd Corps command with the reference number and we see the date. And all I'm trying to establish from this witness is whether the second order from the 3rd Corps issued is within the time period provided by number 4 of the General Staff order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The objection is overruled.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you, Mr. Hasanagic, having just seen that the order provided in the General Staff order was the 18th of July at 8.00 in the evening, could you tell, looking at your own report, whether the 3rd Corps attempted to comply with the order from the General Staff in time.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what was written or I can't recall what was written in the 3rd Corps command's order. My report was to the effect that I am ready, that all the preparations for combat were done, and that I am seeking further instructions from the corps. This is a report, not an order. And the corps command demanded that I send them a report, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. If we look at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, I am -- I think in support of the witness's answer, you will see that this first paragraph, which is the only one I'm able to see of the report, talks in the future. So it is not reporting an accomplished fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is saying -- it is telling you what will happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. Correct.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So in order to establish what happened, I want to show you Exhibit 444, please. And I'm interested in the first page and the time provided and date provided there. First of all, have you -- do you recall having been shown this document?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So if you look here, the time period is the 18th of July, 10.00. Thinking about the General Staff order, would you believe that this order for the continuation of attacking engagement Proljece is within the time period initially set by the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is a coincidence because this is a continuation of the Proljece operation from May 1995 and this coincided with the General Staff's and 3rd Corps commander's orders. Because Proljece II is supposed to be commenced on the 21st -- 20th and 21st July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: But you agree with me that you issued that order at that time here, 18th of July, 10.00 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. I will move on to other topics. We were -- or my learned colleague was discussing reports from the El Mujahedin Detachment being sent to you. And this is transcript 3155, line 1. You responded to one of the questions of my learned colleague: "It was a precedent in the division if reports did not come in, and the division meted out severe punishments towards units who failed to submit their reports." Do you remember having said that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you explain to the Chamber which severe punishments were you referring to.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would send a warning. We demanded that the chief of staff or the commander to report to the command post or to a place specified to explain why they hadn't done it, and they had to write the report regardless of the circumstances obtaining -- well, "punishment" is maybe too harsh a word, but measures were taken. Let's put it this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And in terms of continued non-compliance, what measures were you then having at your disposal?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Another warning would be sent. This is what fell within my purview. I did not have authority to punish in some other way. After written warnings, they would comply.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. And against which units did you impose such measures you were just reporting about?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Against the units within my composition and against the El Mujahedin Detachment, I would send warnings, reminders to all of them, and I was very clear in my warnings that I could not be in a position to report to my superior command or prepare any other kinds of support -- reports if I did not know the state of affairs in my subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Then in response to the question for oral reports by my learned colleague, oral reports from the El Mujahedin Detachment command, you responded -- this is transcript page 3105, lines 1 till 18: "There was analysis after the completion of the Proljece action and they were present at that analysis briefing."

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Where was this analysis meeting after Operation Proljece taking place?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After Proljece operation, who attended were reports from the 3rd Corps -- representatives from the 3rd Corps at the command post of the 35th Division.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Which was at the time where?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command post of the division in Zavidovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And which units apart from the 3rd Corps attended?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the units that took part in the Proljece operation: The 3rd, 4th, 5th Mechanised Battalion, the 328th, 329th Brigades, units from the 3rd Corps, the 2nd Mechanised Battalion, and the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I note the translation says "Mechanised Battalion." Could we clarify. Are we talking about manoeuvre battalions? This is page 55 --

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Manoeuvre. I apologise. Manoeuvre battalions. I apologise. My mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And who from the El Mujahedin Detachment took place?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Took place?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who attended from the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- Aiman, the interpreter, and there was another person who introduced himself as the commander. I can't remember the name. I can't remember the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. Can I have PT2143 being shown to the witness, please. We see it's an order from the 7th of June, 1995 entitled "Participation of the El Mujahedin Detachment in offensive combat operations." My first question is: Have you ever seen the document?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't seen it until now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yeah. I have, nevertheless, selected this document for today because you are mentioned indirectly, I believe, in paragraph 3 of the attachment. If we can scroll down in the English -- in B/C/S, please, a little bit. And in English, it is page 2. And I'll give you time to read it.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a report, an analysis, better said.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Would -- do you remember the event being stated here?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What do you mean by "I think it was"? I don't understand your answer. Can you explain, please.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This analysis took place as after each combat activity. I believe that this analysis did take place, and now we have a document testifying to that effect, and this is only normal in our procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And here it mentions a name of the El Mujahid commander, and I'm just asking you: Have you ever heard that name, Abu Maali Hasan?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did hear about that name.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who is -- or what have you heard about that name?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said yesterday, when they introduced -- when they came here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, at this point, the Prosecutor is not dealing with redirect. He is restating his questions during his examination-in-chief. This should have been explained during direct examination and now the Prosecutor is re-opening his direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm just mentioning it because it says here in the third line of the third paragraph that this person reported to the commander of the 35th Division. "Reported," it says here. That's why I am inquiring.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He did not report --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah. Yeah, just a -- just a second. Just a second, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah, but the problem is do you -- what -- what was the reason that this document was not shown to the -- to the witness during examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Prosecution had so many documents to show, and this is not a document which was authored by this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So the reason for showing other documents was that the Prosecution focused on documents signed by this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: By this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And now on cross-examination the issue of reporting, including oral reporting has come up. And here is hearsay information, if I may state, about oral reporting to the 35th Division commander. That's why it was selected at this late stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. I'll allow the question. Yes -- oh, sorry, yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may -- may be heard before that. First of all, I cross-examined on the issue of reports both written and oral prompted and covered by the Prosecutor during his examination-in-chief. So this was my cross. This was not a new element that I introduced in my cross-examination. I did not introduce a new fact. The Prosecutor examined in detail the receipt of reports during his examination-in-chief. And a practical consequence of what the Prosecutor is doing when they fail to show such documents to the witness is that in my cross-examination I am in no position to ask proper questions to the witness. So, please, I did not broach the issue of reports in my cross-examination. That issue was broached by the Prosecutor during his direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. The objection is overruled. The question is allowed. You may respond later, Madam Vidovic, if you so wish. You can apply to -- to re-- to cross-examine again on this point specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you -- what have you learned about Abu Maali Hasan?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was introduced to me as the Emir of the unit. I learned about Hasan for the first time here, but he was not introduced as the commander. This is my knowledge about him in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: When was he introduced to you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was introduced to him by Aiman when he delivered the plan on the 15th of May. Maybe on that occasion, maybe even earlier, but I can't recall and pinpoint.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The 15th of May, 1995?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I say, maybe then, maybe earlier. I can't really be specific about the time when he said this to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And could you describe Mr. Maali, Abu Maali?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was tall. And what distinguished him from the rest is that he did not sport a beard. Sometimes maybe a short one or a stubble, but he did not sport a long beard, contrary to all the others. And this is what I remember him by; he did not wear a beard.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I would show you a picture, would you be in a position to recognise him?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: With the usher's assistance, if, please, PT6166 could be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I want my objection to enter the record. The Prosecutor has re-opened examination-in-chief again. This attempt at identifying somebody should have been done in his examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I am in the Court's hands. I can withdraw showing that picture, but stating what the witness has said for the first time, that now he's told me that he has seen Abu Maali, I can explore this angle for the first time. Before, when the video - I'm referring to Exhibit 409 - was shown, the witness had not told me that he has seen Abu Maali. So I am now in a different situation, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, yeah, it goes to preparation -- Just a second. Just a second, sir. It goes to preparation. Why do you get surprised by your witness in court? I don't think the identification of a picture goes to the question of reporting. I think you must stay within the question of reporting.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. I do. Okay, I withdraw the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Then I will move on just - and I have a few final questions - to something you stated when Exhibit 486 was shown to you. And this is transcript page 3131, line 12: "The only one who introduced himself when he came to my command was Moatez. He was the military commander," you answered. Could you explain to me -- you said "he was the military commander" of which unit?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When they came here, he was the only one who introduced himself. He said, "I am Moatez, the military commander of the El Mujahedin Detachment."

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And so he introduced himself to you. Could he speak your language?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, when he came to my office with Aiman, I asked the interpreter, "Who's this now?" And then Aiman said, "This is the military commander." And that person confirmed that. And this is how I know that. As I told you - and I reiterate - in the contact of the El Mujahedin Detachment and their members, there was always this linguistic barrier. And the only person who communicated with them and with us was this person Aiman, who was the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And when did Aiman come with Moatez to your office?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really pinpoint the time. I'm not sure whether this was in my office or maybe out in the field. I can't really recall the time and the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you remember what are you discussed with Mr. Moatez on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We discussed combat activities. We discussed military matters. I can't really specify right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And then you stated - this is on transcript page 3131, line 24 - "I had contacts with Aiman on several occasions." Could you tell briefly when these contacts started with Mr. Aiman.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the corps chief of staff brought him to me for the first time and introduced him as a member of the El Mujahedin Detachment, and he told me that I would be maintaining contacts with him, and that he spoke our language.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Which -- this chief of staff was from which corps?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you know his name?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that Kadir Jusic was the chief of staff at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If we look at Exhibit 429 - the last document I'm showing today - for a second. We see the document is from the 23rd of October, 1994. And I ask you to look at number 1, please. If the English could be scrolled down. Is -- here the chief of staff mentioned. Is that the occasion you were just reporting about?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yeah. Could you just clarify one issue. It talks at the very end in brackets, after the name "El Mujahedin Detachment command" is mentioned, in brackets, "About 10 people."

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see them. I saw only Aiman together with the chief of staff and the intelligence officer from the corps and the operatives from the corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Madam Vidovic, do you want to exercise your right to deal with that document?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Sorry, I forgot to tender the map into evidence. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The map is lying next to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Oh. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'd rather cross-examine during -- after the break, because we are going to print out that document. In the meantime, if you concur -- or maybe after your questions, if you agree, I would be dealing with that document because I had no occasion to prepare it. I would like to see the entire document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You can deal with the question and questions arising from the Bench. Okay? Is that okay? Okay. Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The map, yes. I'm -- I'm remembering. May the map -- map 3 from the binder please be admitted into evidence and be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 507.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Also the document just shown to the witness with the PT number 2143, if I could ask that this document is please admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May PT2143 also be admitted into evidence and be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 508.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Fine. Judge? Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, to your knowledge, were there any Mujahedins that were foreigners in the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know the establishment of the 7th Muslim, and they were not anywhere near my units, so I can't really answer this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. You told us that you don't really know anything about the composition of the El Mujahedin Detachment. You couldn't give us the exact number of soldiers that composed this detachment. We saw a document, however, today. It was confirmed to us that the document was only a work document. And in that document, we saw a figure of 600 members, soldiers. I understand that it's only a work document, but how can one put a number relating to soldiers in a work document if no precise information existed to that effect? Can you explain to us why does this figure appear?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Many corps command orders that reached us would specify the detachment, using 10, 150, 200, 250, 350 members, and it is correct, as you point out, the largest number was 600. But I was never sure. Those figures came from the corps. And whenever I asked Aiman about the head count, he would retort formulaically, "En-Shala, God willing, there will be enough brothers." So I never knew exact answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for this explanation. That's all. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. General, I have a number of questions and I will just put a few of them to you in -- before the break here and then we will continue after the break. One of the short questions that I have relate to the lawyer whom you mentioned in your earlier testimony. And I understand that this was a lawyer attached to the command of the 35th Division. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: What was his functions? What did he do? What -- which kind of advice did he offer?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He offered legal advice to officers, soldiers. We discussed orders that reached us. He would explain the orders reaching us from our superior command. He monitored the regulations which concerns the division, units, and soldiers. He followed regulations, in terms of international law, as concerned our division; meaning codes of conduct, codes of military conduct. Of course -- and, of course, he cooperated with the security organ whenever disciplinary measures were meted out and other measures were taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know if he was -- if he had received any training in the international humanitarian law? Was he knowledgeable about the contents of the Geneva Conventions, for instance?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do believe that they went to Zenica to attend some seminars, but I really cannot tell you anything detailed about that. But I believe he took part in drafting the final versions of orders by inputting the elements that you just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. I think we can take the break now and then I will just continue my line of questions after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge. Please come back at half past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Judge, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes. General, we were speaking about the assistance of the lawyer that was attached to the command of the 35th Division. My question, to continue with this lawyer, is: Do you know if he was ever engaged in the investigation or prosecution of any crimes committed by any member of the 35th Division?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall. He cooperated with the security organs, but to what extent, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Were you given information by the lawyer or by the security -- the chief of security or by anyone else, for that matter, of such investigations being made at all?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't -- no, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So to your recollection, no investigations were made -- criminal investigations were made against any member of the 35th Division in 1995.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, as you are aware, I'm sure, this trial relates to the activities of the El Mujahedin Detachment, and it is for this reason extremely important for the Chamber to elicit as much information as we can about the control over the El Mujahedin Detachment, so I'm going to put a number of questions to you regarding this issue. First of all, was it your recollection that you -- that you, as commander of the 35th Division, had control over the members of the El Mujahid Detachment after it had been subordinated to you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not and I could not have control over them because I did not have enough information and everything else that we discussed so that I could have control over that detachment. Starting with the establishment, head count, reporting, and the other elements that are of very great importance for me having any control over them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, General. I'm glad that you mentioned yourself a few of the issues that would be relevant to the issue of control; namely, the establishment of the El Mujahid Detachment, the head counts, the reporting, and so on, because my next question is: What do you mean by the word "control"? And let me be more precise: If you as a military leader were to describe to me what "command and control" means in military terms, what would your answer be?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The element of command is control, and I should know how, in which way they prepare for combat activity, how and in which way they carry out combat activities, because that is why they came to the area of responsibility in most cases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So what you are saying is that you should be informed at least about their preparation for combat and their conduct of combat.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and the success they achieved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: To what level of detail would you be able to control their activities during combat?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once combat activity starts if it is an attack then from the initial positions, how they reached the target of their action, what they are supposed to do at that facility that they had taken, that was their target, and also the continuation of combat activity, if required.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But otherwise you would leave it to the -- the commander of that unit to -- to control the activities of the combatants in the field?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was responsible for a certain task, for a certain axis, to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Now, you said a while ago that you did not have control over the Mujahid Detachment. And this is -- it appears to be, at least, some sort of a contradiction because, on the one hand, you had the El Mujahid Detachment at your disposal and you did, in fact, use them in combat, yet you maintain that you had no command over them. How am I to understand this?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The way I would put it is "under my control," not "had no command over them." I could not control some of their actions, because I didn't have any reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Which actions are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am referring to combat activities, action in terms of combat activity; what they were doing at that place, how much time they were spending there and so on, because they had been given an orientational task and it is that facility that is the target. Now, how they would get to that facility or target is something that I could not control.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So am I to conclude on the basis of your testimony that you had command over the El Mujahedin Detachment but you had no control over them? Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the order, the re-subordination order, I was supposed to command them. But in terms of the execution of tasks, I could not because I did not ... Or rather, in terms of the paperwork, they were re-subordinated to me so that I command them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: If -- let us just take this as a hypothesis. If it were brought to your attention that members of the El Mujahid Detachment had committed war crimes during combat operations, would you then have felt that you would be responsible for those crimes?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would take measures, inform the corps command, and certainly I would have been partly responsible for what they had done, because it's my area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I accept that. Now, let's look at a slightly different aspect of the activities of the El Mujahid Detachment. You told us yesterday that from time to time the El Mujahid Detachment would ask you for engineering support. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Would they also ask for other kind of support, like provision of ammunition, medical assistance, and other forms of assistance from the 35th Division?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 35th Division had a war hospital, and they asked to have their soldiers and wounded be brought to this hospital that was under the 35th Division. Also, they wanted to prepare facilities for activity. I explained logistics support yesterday. It was at their level and the corps intervened in terms of the equipment that they did not have. I myself did not have enough equipment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: We will come to their equipment in just a minute, but -- but speaking of -- of assistance and services offered to the Mujahid Detachment by the 35th Division, my question would also be: If you had arranged religious services and if the members of the Mujahid Detachment took part in those religious services.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not organise that. I did not organise that in the division.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Were religious ceremonies held within the ambit of the 35th Division? I mean, were there masses given or anything of that kind?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within the 35th Division, the command of the 35th Division, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's look then at the weaponry available to the 35th Division. You have told us that you had not been informed of what the El Mujahid Detachment really had in terms of weaponry.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that when we asked for operations records, they did not give me the list of weapons and ammunitions that was prescribed under those rules and records.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I understand. But did you have intelligence or other information available to you to show what they actually had? For instance, did you know if they had mortars? Did they have tanks? Did they have other artillery?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In one plan, they mentioned a few weapons that they had available. I remember these were mortars, light launchers, and some anti-armour weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I think at one point earlier this morning there was one of the documents referring to the El Mujahid providing a tank platoon. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the corps that gave the tank platoon to the El Mujahid. The division did not have any tanks. It said: "The El Mujahid Detachment with one tank platoon," and that tank platoon came from the corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Does a tank platoon come with a tank also?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, three tanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So the -- the 3rd Corps would deliver three tanks to the El Mujahid Detachment? Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says in the order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Very well. You also mentioned in your earlier testimony that the El Mujahid Detachment enjoyed some sort of protection from what you called "the clergy." I would like you to expand a bit on this. What sort of protection are we speaking about and who was "the clergy"?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read this piece of information just before this. They, together with the religious officials in the territory of Zavidovici, they had contact and they probably went to pray with them. They attended these religious rites. I did not attend. Exceptionally, only when there was a big holiday like Bajram, then I was invited. That was organised by the religious officials in Zavidovici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I see. But what did you mean by "protection"? General, you may freely speak up and -- and give us your impression of the status that the EMD, the El Mujahid Detachment, enjoyed in your view.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my view and according to the information that exists, it was stated there that the current leadership trusted the EMD more than the division command. Is that the result of the fact that we had the kind of composition of division that we had, that we were not organised from a religious point of view, that we did not have a particular religious affiliation or whether they knew something that I did not know? But that's the information and the report that exists. And the division command got more distant from me, and I noticed that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: You said - and I am just quoting you from the transcript now - that the current leadership trusted the El Mujahid Detachment more than the division command. What do you mean by this?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I read in their report that I came across. That report exists. I would not know what they meant by that, but I know that at one point in time they said - in that report, that is - that the division is a burden for them and that it should leave Zavidovici. Of course, I didn't know about it then. I was preoccupied with combat activities and I did not pay much attention to what I've been telling you just now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Who are "they"? Who is the current leadership that you are talking about?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The current authorities in the town of Zavidovici. Perhaps even beyond that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Are you suggesting that -- that it would reach higher up, beyond and above the religious leadership in Zavidovici?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said the then-current authorities in Zavidovici asked that of the higher instances. That is what the document says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Very well. Let's move to Exhibit 504, if we can, please, because I noticed that in the bottom, if you look at the units which were informed about the establishment of the new forward command post in Livade, I think I did not see that the El Mujahid Detachment had been informed of this, and that surprised me, if it is true. You are setting up a new forward command post, but you're not informing, if I'm correct, the -- if I am -- if I have understood this correctly, you're not informing the El Mujahid Detachment. Why not?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This pertains to the combat activity that is moving towards Maglaj. Because the corps commander already then, in terms of one of the coordinations - I think it was either the 15th or the 16th - he already started issuing orders to the EMD independently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So you -- if I understand you correctly, the El Mujahid Detachment would not be involved in -- in these combat activities and, therefore, need not be informed of the establishment of that forward command post; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if the EMD took part in this here, but I did not issue any orders to them any more. That's why they are not here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Oh, I see. It was after their -- they had been, so to say, subordinated back to the 3rd Corps. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even before that. Even before the order of the 23rd. Could it please be scrolled up so that I see the heading. Yes, yes, it was before the 23rd, because in this order it says, "when the need ceases or on the 23rd."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I apologise. I'm not sure I completely understand here. You said that you had stopped giving them orders. Why did you stop giving them orders when the corps had not yet taken the El Mujahid Detachment back from you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I either didn't know where they were or the corps commander took them under him. I really cannot respond to this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But on the 17th of September, they were still under your command, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the order that will follow, yes. But from this, we see -- well, the commander issued the order to them himself or I did not know where they were, so I could not give them a task.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I see. So it was a question of giving a task to them. But could there have been any other reason why you would not inform them of the establishment of the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then I received the task, as far as I can remember, to take the lines, and it's probably that I concentrated only on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, General. My last question relates to the reason why the El Mujahid Detachment was re-subordinated from the 3rd Corps to you. Do you know?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, the division's area of responsibility is something that I talked about a few times. It was really the most difficult theatre of war in that area, not only in terms of the configuration of the terrain but also in terms of the enemy forces that were concentrated there. They wanted to keep the area of Vozuca at all costs and their forces were concentrated in that area the most. That is one thing. Secondly, in that area - that is to say, Maglaj, Zavidovici - it was an inhabited area. The population hadn't gone anywhere and they were constantly under fire. In the zone of responsibility of my division, during the course of that one year, over 25 corps units came at different times to help the division. At that time, the most active theatre of war and where the forces were concentrated - the corps forces, that is - was the zone of this division. I repeat, due to the fact that this zone was so difficult, the situation was so special there, due to the significance of the roads and the area of Vozuca, the road between Zavidovici and Ribnica -- or rather, Zenica-Tuzla, all of that gave importance to the area of responsibility of the 35th Division. And it so happened it was not of my own accord that I came to that area. I was ordered to go there and I did what I could.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge. I'm sorry to have to go through some of the issues that have already been traversed, but I'm trying to approach them from a completely different -- a slightly different angle. This morning you testified about measures that you would take if members of the unit that were subordinated to you did not carry out orders. You remember that? You said --

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They would submit reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't understand that answer. I'm just trying to orientate you. I'm trying to turn to -- to direct your attention to your testimony this morning when you told the Chamber that -- about the measures that you used to take when members of your subordinated units did not carry out orders. I'm asking you: Do you remember that part of the testimony this morning?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We discussed their failure to submit reports on combat activities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Right. Now, I'm talking generally, just when your units -- subordinated units did not -- did not carry out instructions you said you sent them warnings and you repeated the warning. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That -- I want you to think about that. I know that the Prosecutor asked you what you would do in a situation where non-compliance with instructions continued. And can you just remind me, what did you say what would you do?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seems to me that I said that I would undertake disciplinary measures. I would summon the commanders to report or to a meeting. I personally warned them about the gravity of the situation, not this time to the whole commands but to the commanders themselves, and gave instructions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you've told us about the number of times, many times when the El Mujahedin Detachment did not comply with instructions. Did you summon them for -- summon their commanders to come and did they come?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did invite. Most frequently Aiman would come and one Moatez appeared.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So they -- they did finally obey your orders. Is that -- is that what you are saying? Because now when you called them, they do come.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This situation arose once and they appeared.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And did they give you a satisfactory explanation of their conduct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They said -- well, I can relate what they told to me: "En-Shala, God willing, everything is going to be okay." This was their response. I could not really do much or maintain frequent contacts with them or try to prevail over them the same way that I succeeded in prevailing upon the commander of the 4th Manoeuvre Battalion when I threatened him that he would be replaced. My purview and my authority powers were not such that I could threaten the same threat to the EMD.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do I -- do I understand from that answer that in fact you were not satisfied with their response?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And when you were not satisfied with their response, what did you do with the situation?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I informed the corps command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we please have Exhibit 455 on the screen. Could we -- could we -- how many pages is this document? I'm sorry, I -- I'm not quite sure of the page I'm looking for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm looking for -- for the page that deals with the El Mujahedin Detachment refusing to forward prisoners of war and documents. If -- Mr. Registrar, if you are able to help us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I may assist, it is number 6 in the order, and it's page 7 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And page 3 -- the last page, actually, of the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. If you might remind me. I don't want to go back to page 1. Mr. -- Mr. Hasanagic, this document is addressed to?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Addressed to the corps command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And this would be an example of the action you took where you were not able to -- to resolve the problem yourself. You would then report to the 3rd Corps -- the corps commander?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you know if the corps commander did do anything about this specific problem that you reported of prisoners and captured documents not being handed over?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible that he did it directly, because he had communication with the El Mujahedin Detachment and maybe the relevant organs from the command of the corps did something, but I did not personally receive any advice or information about what the command did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are speculating. Are you speculating? I don't want you to speculate. I'm just asking -- my question really was: Do you know? If you don't know, just say you don't know.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know. I apologise. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Okay. You -- you also testified, sir, about the fact that you never knew anything about the establishment of the Mujahedin, their numbers and all those things. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But you also said, in response to a question from the Defence, that you do know that not all the Mujahedins that operated in Central Bosnia were part of the El Mujahedin Detachment. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I was a bit surprised at that, because if you don't know the strength of the El Mujahedin Detachment, how -- how do you know that any Mujahedin that you see is not a member of the El Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I answered your question to the effect that they did not wear insignia and that apart from them, that there were units in Zeljezno -- I mean there were Arabs also in Zeljezno Polje, it seems to me, in Tesanj and in Zavidovici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Who did not wear insignia?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did not wear the army's insignia. The El Mujahedin Detachment did not wear such insignia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's right. Now, if you didn't -- that's precisely my point. They didn't wear the insignia of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Now, did those Mujahedin that you say were not members of the El Mujahedin Detachment, did they wear any distinctive signs?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So then my question, then, is just that: How -- how do you know that there are Mujahedin out there in somewhere Central Bosnia who are not members of the El Mujahedin Detachment if you do not know the establishment of the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know the establishment of the detachment, but I know that they were established as part of the 3rd Corps. This, I did say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are -- sorry, you are not answering my question, unless you say -- unless you don't understand my question. Let me try -- do you want me to try and put it to you differently? Maybe -- maybe I'm not coming across clearly. I am saying you don't know the establishment -- the establishment of the El Mujahedin Detachment. You see Mujahedins all over Bosnia and Herzegovina. How do you know that a particular Mujahedin is or is not a member of the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So when you then said that you do know that not all Mujahedin in Central Bosnia belonged to the El Mujahedin Detachment, you couldn't have been correct. Were you mistaken?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably I was mistaken. But what I did say is that I heard from civilians that there were Mujahedin in those places, locations that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may have said that. Maybe it slipped me. But I think I'm hearing that for the first time. I didn't get the impression that you said you got this knowledge from information from civilians.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I did. I can't recall really.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. That's fine. Let's leave it at that point. At least you have given me an answer. You testified about a meeting that you had with the commander of the army and, I think you said, the command of the corps when you saw Mujahedin in the corridor, the El Mujahedin -- some El Mujahedin people in the corridor. Do you remember that testimony?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw Aiman only, but policemen who were there or soldiers who were there, as they said to me later, "We had seen some Mujahedin."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Am I right to say that you also testified that you were not -- you cannot say whether they did or did not talk to the commander of the army and the commander of the 3rd Corps on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I could not say whether they did or they did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And you also said that you were the host of these two gentlemen.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: As the host, were you not with them until when they left and saw them off?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't with them for a period of time, but I did see them off, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Oh, it was just for a period of time that you were not with them.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How long a period of time? Are you able to say?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's difficult for me to remember. 15-odd minutes. Difficult to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Can I follow up on certain answers that you gave this morning to Judge Harhoff. You -- you just said in answer to his questions that the El Mujahedin Detachment obtained a tank platoon from the 3rd Corps, got the tanks, three tanks, from the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You also indicated yesterday in testimony that the El Mujahedin Detachment was -- did not accept assistance from you. They didn't accept assistance from you and they didn't give you reports of what arms and ammunition they had.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not submit reports on weapons and munition except for that one occasion when they proposed the plan for the Proljece operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sure. I understand. But generally, they didn't give you these reports.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And generally they didn't accept assistance from you.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, based on this -- these three tanks that they were given, is it fair to infer that they were getting assistance from somewhere else within the army outside your 35th Division?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I could not say generally, but for that specific and particular mission, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's the specific mission that you are aware of.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Every time you gave them orders to go to combat, they went to combat, even without tanks.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But without you having given them any arms.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Doesn't that suggest they must get the arms elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I said that they must have received and be supplied with equipment some -- from somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And I am mindful of a document that was shown to you indicating that they received money from -- from some NGOs. I'm mindful of that, but -- but I'm asking --

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and this is what I saw for the first time yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's true. But it's just that now you're talking about this -- these tanks that came from the 3rd Corps. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise for interrupting, but the witness's testimony was not to the effect that the tanks came from the 3rd Corps but that he saw an order stating that. And you can -- may check the transcript. You can see that he did not say that he saw the tanks coming. This is a completely different thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We don't need to look at the transcript. I accept that and let's just clear it up. You -- it's your testimony, sir, that you are not saying you saw the tanks but you saw an order allocating tanks to the El Mujahedin Detachment? Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was this order. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, you also said to Judge Harhoff that you wanted to exercise control and be able to see what they do in action. When you were -- they were engaged in that operation where they were using the tanks -- or did you see the tanks?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I was exercising control, but I did not see those tanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You did not see the tanks. Okay. Can we just go to a couple of pages backwards. You may have answered this question to Judge Harhoff, but I'm not quite sure I heard you. When you said the current leadership trusted the EMD more than the division command, did you say that leadership was the clergy in Zavidovici or was it somebody else?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the authorities at Zavidovici. The then-current authorities in Zavidovici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. And then you also said that the then-current authorities in Zavidovici asked that of the higher instances. That's at page 74, line 1. If I may just --

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Right. And who are the higher instances or what are the higher instances?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The authorities that functioned in this State of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah. You see, you -- you have told us about the authorities in Zavidovici. Now, the higher authorities in the State of Bosnia and Herzegovina, which ones specifically? Which operate at which level?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember specifically which level. First, the canton and then the federation -- no, the canton and the republic or the state. I can't recall how it functions at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. But are we then to -- to deduce from your evidence that you are saying not only did they enjoy the -- or let me -- let me ask you a question first: Did the higher instances then accede to the request of the authorities from Zavidovici?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not. I remained the chief of that division until the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did not accede. I remained in my position and division remained in Zavidovici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What had been the request of the -- these authorities? That you be removed? I thought -- I thought you were talking about the protection. We were talking -- we were talking with Judge Harhoff about the protection that was afforded the El Mujahedin Detachment by the authorities in Zavidovici and that the -- the authorities in Zavidovici asked that of higher instances.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said they believed the EMD more than they did the command of the 35th Division.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Who? The -- who? The authorities of Zavidovici?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And did the authorities at higher instance also believe the EMD more than the -- they believed the division?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's Correction: Trust more than, not believe more. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did the higher instances also trust the EMD more than the division?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I don't know that. But the information that was sent from Zavidovici did not have the desired effect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Finally, you did say also at page 74 today, lines 14 to 16, that the corps commander already then, in terms of one of the coordinations, already started issuing orders to the EMD independently.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you able to give a time line as to when you first noticed that he gave these orders directly without coming via you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this was after the 12th, when activities started towards the north -- north and Blizna, and particularly when it -- we accomplished the Blizna target, around the 15th or 16th, and beyond that date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 15th and 16th of ...?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: September.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. And -- [Previous translation continues] ... --

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah, finish off. Finish off what you wanted to say, sir.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And as early as on the 11th and the 12th, during the coordination meetings, activities towards the north were being directed by the corps commander himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I just want to follow up on a few questions made by Your Honour Harhoff about command and control of the El Mujahedin Detachment, particularly in combat situations. And this is page 68 and 69 of today's transcript. Further re-examination by Mr. Neuner:

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to show you a document, Exhibit 449. And I'm particularly interested in number 1 of that document. We see it's from the 16th of July, 1995, that document. Could you explain briefly to which combat operations the document may relate to.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Proljece II.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And if you look at number 1, you see that there are a couple of persons at the command post of the El Mujahedin Detachment here. And I'm referring to the commander of the 328th Mountain Brigade and the commander of the 329th Mountain Brigade and the commander of the 5th Manoeuvre Battalion. And then there are a few persons, as you can see, who represent at this command post the 35th Division. I'm referring to Muharem Ismicic. Who is Muharem Ismicic?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Operations officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Of the 35th Division.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And who is Eniz Omicevic?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Operations officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And Suad Hasagic?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is from the moral guidance organ.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And then it says here: "The tasks of these officers," in the following sentence, "will be to offer necessary assistance for RiK using their troops and to carry out the requested" - it's a little bit illegible here - "and through the 35th Division." Could you explain what is meant here.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If some assistance is required, in terms of command and control, this group of people can help. And if something should be resolved among the units -- or rather, the commanders of these units; and if some requests are to be addressed to the command of the 35th Division. Normal activity, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to show you another document, Exhibit 464, the document from the 6th of September, 1995 we can see here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, these questions that are put by the Prosecutor -- or rather, the one that he put in relation to the previous document, that is the document that he brought in during the examination-in-chief. He dealt with it. I cross-examined on it. And I used this document for that. If anything had remained uncleared, he could have dealt with it during the re-examination. The questions that he put in relation to the previous document did not come from the questions put by His Honour Judge Harhoff at all. These questions were clearly answered by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I -- Mr. Harhoff had inquired how command and control was exercised during combat operations, and I just wanted to dwell on this one particular point. If Your Honours believe it is not necessary, I'm prepared to move on. I believe it relates exactly to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I must say that I put a question to the witness. The witness gave his answer. And let's just leave it at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So I think you should move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Then I want to just clarify another issue relating to Judge Harhoff's questions and a document which was shown from the 17th of September, 1995. It's page 74 and 75 of today's transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And the question was whether the El Mujahedin Detachment were at this time still under your control or under the control of the 3rd Corps, if I remember correctly now. I just wanted to show you a document, Exhibit 479, which is from about the same time period. We can see here in the B/C/S it's from the 22nd of September, 1995, five days later. And I'm interested in the second-last paragraph of B/C/S; and in the English, it's page 3 of the translation. If you look at the second-last paragraph, it says here that some 80 soldiers have been re-subordinated to the El Mujahedin Detachment. How would you describe looking at this information the situation of command and control over the El Mujahedin Detachment on the 22nd of September, 1995?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am talking about our forces and I am giving orders to my 328th Brigade, and that is the time when the corps commander's order came, on that day or the next day when the EMD was taken out of my composition. This is an order to my 328th Brigade because that brigade was supposed to take up lines and I ordered them in relation to these forces; where reference is made to Ozren, indepth, how difficult this front line is, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you are re-subordinating 80 soldiers from the 328th Brigade to the El Mujahedin, how would you describe the relationship to the El Mujahedin Detachment in this moment?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is already a corps unit. It will carry out this task as a corps unit and that is why I am re-subordinating my forces to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will have some questions. Could the witness please have a look at Exhibit 508. Actually, Your Honour, before we get to that, could the witness please first look at PT2389 in order to have an easier understanding of what it is that I wish to look at. Further cross-examination by Ms. Vidovic:

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Hasanagic, could you please look at this document. Your Honours, I tried to get this document to understand what Mr. Hasanagic is speaking about. I believe that this Defence document was supposed to come in accordance with Rule 68, but we located it as PT and its date is the 12th of August, 1995. And it says: "The army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the 3rd Corps, the security department," and what is referred to are areas -- are relations in the area of responsibility of the 35th Division and it's sent to the security administration of the army. Mr. Hasanagic, before you answer some questions related to these documents -- or rather, this document, I would like to ask you the following: In response to the questions put by His Honour Judge Moloto, you mentioned the authorities in general in Zavidovici and then you said it can be the canton, the republic. I'm asking you now to give a precise answer. What is it that you were referring to here? Civilian authorities that protected the Mujahedin from Zavidovici and the cantons, or is it military authorities? Could you tell us that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Civilian structures of authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I see. And then further on, when you said "several authorities in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina," did you -- or rather, "higher authority in Bosnia-Herzegovina," did you refer to the military or civilian authorities?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Civilian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Please, now I'd like to draw your attention to this document. Do you agree -- or rather, first of all, I believe that the Prosecutor showed you this document during your proofing, because you keep talking about this document, this report about relations in the field. But anyway, I wish to ask you the following: Please look at the second sentence here. It says: "The civilian structures express their distrust in the division command, considering it a burden for Zavidovici municipality." Is that the document that you were referring to, that you had seen it?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Please look further down, and you will see -- Your Honours, I believe -- well, could the English version please be scrolled down so that you can see this in English. "Asim Camdzic," can you see that name? Please go to page 2 in English. Look at this, Mr. Hasanagic. This is what it says: "In terms of individuals from the SDA said" - that's the Party of Democratic Action; right -- "some SDA members were openly belittling the results of the units of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and they were glorifying the results of the Asim Camdzic unit and the El Mujahedin Detachment at religious gatherings, which created a certain amount of distrust among citizens in the commands of the units of the BH army." And now a bit further down, could you have a look. It says: "The lack of SDA political activity in the field, which would throw light on the objectives of our fight, the mobilisation of conscripts," and so on and so forth, and many problems that the 35th Division had with the civilian authorities of Zavidovici is -- are being referred to. Mr. Hasanagic, this is actually what I want to ask you: The many documents you saw - and you accept that you were supposed to be in command, but it's on paper - as for the El Mujahedin Detachment, did you have more influence over them or these people here, the civilian authorities, as shown by this document, the civilian authorities of Zavidovici and so on?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My attitude towards the EMD was only of a military nature, in terms of the task that they were supposed to be carrying out.
