As for all the rest, you can see from this piece of information that it is the civilian authorities in the territory of Zavidovici that had influence over them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I don't understand your answer when you say from a military point of view. So from a military point of view, it would mean that they obeyed you? Did they obey your orders or not, Mr. Hasanagic? Please be more specific -- please be clearer. This is not clear, what you've said.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, if you want me to be clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is -- well, I had only two more documents related to documents -- they really are important. Do I have time to continue now and you will remember -- well, they really are important for me. I really wanted to put questions in relation to the Prosecutor's questions. Perhaps not more than six minutes. I'll be very brief, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please go on, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm told we haven't got any other case this afternoon in this court.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Please, Your Honours, could this document please be assigned a number, as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 509.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanagic, please, as for the behaviour of the El Mujahedin unit in combat, except for the fact that this unit was not obedient, they attacked when they wished to, you could not control them. But apart from that fact, did you ever have any knowledge that these people were beating or killing someone? You personally, did you know about that or were you receiving different information?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, now I'd like the witness to have a look at Exhibit 508 that the Prosecutor showed him today. This question is related to Exhibit 508, and the Trial Chamber has allowed me to show it to him; to the witness, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Please, Witness, could you have a look at this document once again, the document shown to you by the Prosecutor today. And you can see that this is a document of the security service department. Do you agree that it is being submitted to the state security centre in Zenica for some reason?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I saw it, I was also surprised what the reason was -- I mean, why it was being sent to them. I don't know what the reason is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You will agree that the police did have authority over everything that is outside army control?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Now, this is something different. We don't have time to discuss it, but here attached to this document is obviously what it says here: "Attachment. Official note." Do you agree that this is an attachment to what was sent to the police?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Now I'm asking you the following: It says here in the first paragraph: "In the most recent offensive operations in the Vozuca battlefield, land forces 35th Division area of responsibility, the El Mujahid detachment was active along the main axis and has fully achieved its task. The detachment's behaviour in completing the combat assignment was fully disciplined and the assignment was carried out with a high surprise factor." Please, does this document not show that the 3rd Corps was receiving information that these people, if they were engaged, then they were disciplined in fighting, in combat? Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what this note refers to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did you perhaps - you personally - send them different information?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This information and reports that I sent, we looked at them. I sent them as they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if at this point in time -- well, you showed today -- actually, Judge Moloto did, His Honour Judge Moloto showed Exhibit 455. I would like the witness to have a look at it for a moment again in relation to the questions put by His Honour Judge Moloto.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you see this document?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Prosecutor showed it to you and then I showed it to you again. And in relation to this, I asked you yesterday: "Please, is it correct that those 11 prisoners who were taken prisoner in June were handed over without any problems to the military police of the 3rd Corps? Did you know of that?" What is referred to here is a problem -- On page 2, Your Honours. Could we show page 2 for a moment and then I'll go back to page 1. Actually, page 3. Sorry about that. For the record, Your Honours, it says "June," and actually it should say "July"." Page 98, line 15. A few moments ago, His Honour Judge Moloto showed you this part where there is a specific reference to problems of access to prisoners of war and documentation. And again you repeated -- I did not get an answer. I did not get an answer from the corps." Please, did you ask, then - may I ask you that - what happened to these 11 prisoners and this problem here? Did you wonder what happened to these people?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My information was that they went to Zenica and that they were exchanged. I have already said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So you knew they were exchanged. Did you ever hear of them being beaten, maltreated, killed?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not receive such information.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we now look at page 1 of this same document for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I would like to ask you to look at number 3, "Morale." 3(a) on page 1. And could we have the English version on too. Could it please be displayed so that you can see 3(a). Could we have the English version as well. Right. Mr. Hasanagic, please, do you agree that here in this part, in the second sentence, it says: "As for combat morale and security, the El Mujahedin unit has great influence and with their morale and way of life they have become a role model to our soldiers"? Now, I want to ask you the following, Mr. Hasanagic: Please, you signed this report; isn't that right? Didn't you sign it?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Well, I believe, Mr. Hasanagic, that you would not have signed this document had you had information about criminal conduct of the EMD, the mistreatment of prisoners, killings. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did you have such information?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have such knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did you ever pass this on to the higher command, the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Vidovic. Mr. Hasanagic, this brings us to the conclusion of your testimony. On behalf of the Trial Chamber, may I thank you for taking time off your schedule to come and testify. You are now excused. You may stand down. Once again, thank you for coming.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And have a --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And have a nice trip back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The matter stands adjourned to Monday, the 1st of October at quarter past 2.00 in the afternoon, Courtroom II. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 1st day of October, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 24 25
